ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account’s biggest missed opportunity is concentrated in the two Non-Brand search campaigns, where impression share is low (33–35%) primarily due to rank loss (51% lost to rank in both), while budgets are not being fully utilized (only ~61–64% utilization). Keyword-level evidence shows multiple high-quality, high-intent terms still losing the majority of auctions to rank (64–70% lost to rank at QS 7.0–8.5), pointing to an Ad Rank/bid/coverage issue more than a pure budget cap. A secondary efficiency issue is spend leaking into low-intent service/policy queries with low QS and very high cost per conversion.
notable_patterns: Non-Brand Search - Flights and Non-Brand Search - Hotels & Packages account for the majority of missed impressions flagged as material: 356,440 and 300,300 missed impressions respectively (cumulative missed share 0.755 across the two).

Both Non-Brand campaigns show the same shape: low search impression share (33% / 35%) with high impression share lost to rank (51% / 51%) and comparatively lower loss to budget (16% / 14%), while budget utilization is only 63.6% / 61.4% (not consistently hitting caps).

High-quality, core intent terms are still rank-limited: e.g., “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) at 34% IS with 66% lost to rank; “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) at 30% IS with 70% lost to rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) at 36% IS with 64% lost to rank.

Waste/drag is visible in low-QS informational/service queries: “flight booking customer service” (QS 4.0) spent £372.28 at £195.94 cost/conv and “hotel cancellation policy” (QS 4.5) spent £279.27 at £116.36 cost/conv. Meanwhile Hotels & Packages has the lowest avg campaign QS at 5.1.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is only 33% with 51% lost to rank (vs 16% lost to budget) and budget utilization at 63.6%, indicating demand exists but coverage is being limited primarily by Ad Rank rather than budget caps. This aligns with high-intent keywords like “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) and “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) still losing 66–70% of impressions to rank.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase competitiveness on the highest-intent ad groups/keywords (bids/targeting structure) while tightening query control to reduce spend on service-intent searches like “flight booking customer service” (QS 4.0; £195.94 cost/conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is 35% with 51% lost to rank (vs 14% lost to budget) and budget utilization at 61.4%, suggesting auctions are being lost due to rank/coverage rather than spend limits. Avg quality score is weak (5.1), and there is identifiable waste on low-intent terms such as “hotel cancellation policy” (QS 4.5; £116.36 cost/conv).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize QS and relevance improvements (ad group/keyword to ad alignment and landing page relevance) on hotel/package intent themes, and add/query-sculpt negatives to remove policy/support intent traffic.

recommendation_cards.title: Push bids/coverage on the highest-intent Non-Brand terms that are losing 64–70% to rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The two material campaigns are rank-limited: Non-Brand Flights IS 33% with 51% lost to rank; Non-Brand Hotels & Packages IS 35% with 51% lost to rank, while budgets aren’t fully utilized (63.6% and 61.4% utilization). At the keyword level, strong QS terms are still heavily rank-limited: “flights to spain” (QS 8.5) has 34% IS and 66% lost to rank; “cheap flights europe” (QS 7.5) has 30% IS and 70% lost to rank; “weekend city breaks” (QS 7.0) has 32% IS and 68% lost to rank; “all inclusive holidays” (QS 8.0) has 36% IS and 64% lost to rank.
recommended_steps: Identify the ad groups containing: “flights to spain”, “cheap flights europe”, “weekend city breaks”, “all inclusive holidays”; increase bids or loosen any bid ceilings specifically on these segments first (not account-wide).
Separate these highest-intent themes into their own tighter ad groups if they are currently blended, so bid increases don’t lift weaker queries.
Monitor impression share lost to rank weekly; keep scaling until lost-to-rank falls materially without ROAS degradation.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: For those four keywords/ad groups: impression share rising from ~30–36% toward 45%+ and lost to rank dropping from ~64–70% toward <50%.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for customer-service/policy intent in Non-Brand (add negatives + route to support elsewhere)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Low-intent service/policy terms are expensive and low-quality: “flight booking customer service” (QS 4.0) spent £372.28 at £195.94 cost/conv; “hotel cancellation policy” (QS 4.5) spent £279.27 at £116.36 cost/conv. These terms also depress overall relevance signals, and Hotels & Packages already has low avg QS (5.1).
recommended_steps: Add intent negatives (e.g., customer service, phone number, contact, cancellation policy, refund policy, complaints) at the appropriate level for Non-Brand campaigns, while confirming they don’t block legitimate “book/quote/deals” intent.
Create a separate, tightly capped ‘Support’ search campaign only if the business needs coverage for these queries (with tailored ads/landing), otherwise exclude entirely.
Review the last 30 days of search terms for ‘policy/refund/cancellation/telephone’ variants and add as negatives in batches.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on Non-Brand campaigns improving from the outliers (£195.94 / £116.36 on the cited terms) and avg quality score for Hotels & Packages moving up from 5.1 toward 6.0+.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix relevance/QS in Hotels & Packages to reduce rank loss (QS is the weak link)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Non-Brand Hotels & Packages has the lowest avg quality score in the account at 5.1 and is simultaneously losing 51% of impressions to rank with only 35% impression share. Keyword-level evidence also indicates QS is strongly tied to impression share (r=0.957) and to lower cost per conversion (r=-0.883) in this dataset, making QS improvement a practical lever for this campaign specifically.
recommended_steps: Restructure Hotels & Packages into tighter ad groups by intent (e.g., ‘all inclusive holidays’ separate from generic ‘packages’) and ensure ads explicitly mirror the core term in headlines/descriptions.
Align final URLs/landing pages to the specific intent cluster (packages vs all-inclusive vs city breaks) to lift expected CTR and landing relevance components of QS.
For any ad groups with QS ≤5, pause or narrow broad matching until query quality improves, then re-expand cautiously.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Hotels & Packages: avg QS moving from 5.1 toward 6.0+, and impression share lost to rank decreasing from 51% toward <45%.

recommendation_cards.title: Clean up negative keyword conflicts so valid demand isn’t self-blocked
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 2 conflicts blocking an estimated 1,790 impressions: negative “jobs” blocks “flight attendant jobs cheap flights europe” (640 blocked impressions) and negative “visa” blocks “weekend city breaks visa requirements” (1,150 blocked impressions) in the two in-scope Non-Brand campaigns.
recommended_steps: Decide intent: if ‘jobs’ and ‘visa requirements’ traffic is not desired, keep the negatives and instead add stricter phrase/exact negatives to prevent accidental blocking of commercial terms (or split into separate ad groups).

If there is value in those research queries, move them into a separate, low-bid ‘Travel info’ campaign/ad group with tailored ad copy and landing pages rather than letting them mix with booking intent.
After edits, re-run the conflicts report to confirm blocked impressions drop from 1,790 toward ~0 for intended keywords.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions from conflicts decreasing from 1,790 to near zero (or remaining blocked intentionally, but without collateral blocking of core commercial keywords).

already_working: Brand Search - UK is highly efficient (ROAS 48.18 on £9,631.08 spend, 790.3 conversions) and is not materially budget-throttled (only 10% lost to budget; 58.5% utilization), so the main opportunity is elsewhere.
Creative coverage is generally solid: 83.3% of ads are rated Excellent/Good (5 of 6), so the primary limiter in Non-Brand is more rank/coverage and query mix than widespread weak ads.

Auction position is not broadly weak versus the named competitors (avg outranking share 61.4% and self top-of-page rate 66.3% vs competitor 53.9%), reinforcing that the bigger issue is Non-Brand rank/coverage at the keyword level rather than an account-wide competitiveness collapse.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Non-brand search is already rank-constrained while not fully spending budget, so the fastest path to incremental conversions is to win more auctions on core, high-intent terms. External market data indicates search demand and spend are rising sharply right now (notably in the UK and Spain), and the exact keyword theme the account is losing on (“flights to spain”) is showing strong recent growth—meaning every week of continued rank loss likely compounds missed volume during an upswing.

supporting_facts.fact: United Kingdom (pilot account market) shows Search Spend Growth QoQ of 22.0% (table: “Market | Search Spend Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share”, p.13).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Rising search spend typically signals intensifying auction pressure. With the account already losing 51% of impressions to rank in its two main Non-Brand campaigns, increasing bids/Ad Rank on the highest-intent segments becomes more urgent to avoid falling further behind as competition ramps.

supporting_facts.fact: Spain shows Search Spend Growth QoQ of 25.0% (table: “Market | Search Spend Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share”, p.14).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This directly heightens urgency for the Flights non-brand problem because the account is explicitly rank-limited on “flights to spain.” If spend is growing fastest in Spain-related searches, the cost of staying under-ranked increases immediately (more competitors bid up the same auctions).

supporting_facts.fact: The keyword “flights to spain” grows from an index of 100 (Q4 2025) to 151 (Q3 2026), i.e., 51% growth (table: “Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This is the account’s cited high-intent term that is still losing the majority of auctions to rank (66% lost to rank at QS 8.5). The market is telling you that the exact query theme is surging, so fixing Ad Rank coverage now is time-sensitive to capture the incremental demand.

supporting_facts.fact: “last minute flights europe” increases from 100 (Q4 2025) to 156 (Q3 2026), i.e., 56% growth (table: “Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Supports urgency to push rank/coverage on high-intent ‘Europe flights/deals’ themes (aligned with the account’s rank-limited non-brand flight terms like “cheap flights europe”). If this cluster is accelerating, rank loss is an immediate opportunity cost.

supporting_facts.fact: Search represents 41% share of category spend (table: “Channel | Share of Category Spend”, p.13).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Reinforces that search is a primary battleground for this vertical; being under-ranked in non-brand search during a growth period is especially costly. It supports prioritizing Ad Rank/QS work vs. diverting effort elsewhere.

supporting_facts.fact: In the competitive set, “Horizon Holidays” has 16% Spend Share and runs across “Search, Social, Video” (table: “Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels”, p.10).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Indicates at least one key competitor is meaningfully funded and multi-channel, which can increase brand presence and click propensity in search auctions. That raises the urgency to defend/expand non-brand search presence by improving Ad Rank (bids/QS) and reducing wasted spend on low-intent queries.

email_copy.subject: GBP 316,559 sitting in Non-Brand: 47.0% lost to rank while budgets aren’t fully used
email_copy.hook:
You’ve got real demand trying to come through your two Non-Brand search campaigns, but you’re effectively showing up about a third of the time — not because the account is out of money, but because you’re being out-ranked in the highest-intent auctions.

The tell is the pattern: meaningful rank loss alongside unspent budget — a fixable combo that can unlock near-term revenue without changing your daily budget of GBP 6,200.
why_now_bullets: UK search auctions are heating up fast: 22.0% Search Spend Growth QoQ — which typically means higher CPC pressure and more lost auctions if rank isn’t addressed now.
Spain is accelerating even faster at 25.0% Search Spend Growth QoQ, and one of your core themes (“flights to spain”) is already where you’re losing coverage.
Demand for that exact theme is surging: “flights to spain” is up 51% (index 100 to 151) — so every week of continued rank loss is missed volume during an upswing.
email_copy.stat_sub: Concentrated in the two Non-Brand search campaigns
email_copy.impact_line: Right now your account is running at 37.84% impression share, with 47.0% lost to rank (vs 15.2% lost to budget). In plain terms: there’s enough budget headroom, but Ad Rank is keeping you from showing on a large portion of high-intent searches — which is why the fastest path to incremental bookings is tightening coverage where intent is strongest and cutting the spend drag that’s pulling relevance down.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-level breakdown of where that GBP 316,559 is being left on the table, so you can see exactly where the gap is concentrated.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the short prioritized fix list — aimed at winning more of the right auctions (rank) while stopping spend from leaking into low-intent service/policy searches that quietly depress performance.
email_copy.working_intro: Also included: the parts of the account that are already in good shape, so changes stay targeted and you don’t “fix” what’s already working.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If you action the rank + query-quality moves below, the payoff shows up quickly as incremental reach — and those added impressions/clicks are the cleanest route to capturing more of that GBP 316,559 without increasing overall budget.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 2-week action plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two concrete time slots (15 minutes). If you’d rather keep it async, reply “plan” and I’ll send the step-by-step priority order to implement.
email_copy.ps: P.S. This isn’t an account-wide competitiveness problem — it’s a Non-Brand coverage problem. That’s why it’s so fixable (and why it’s time-sensitive while demand is rising).
